correctness.rationale: The cone-gluing construction gives an explicit \(G_n\)-equivariant strong deformation retraction \(Y_n\) onto the closed-neighborhood Čech complex, with each apex sent to its unique base barycenter. The pairwise neighborhood intersections have size at most two, so the matched deletion pairs are genuinely free in descending cardinality order and are G-invariant. The complete residual cell incidence is bijective with a right-diagonal triangulation of every square of \(Q_{n+1}\); the parity-coordinate embedding intertwines all translations and coordinate permutations. A translation reflects h=\(\operatorname{wt}(a)\)+\(\operatorname{par}(a)\) cubical coordinates, so the fixed set inside the 2-skeleton is \(2^{n-1}\) square centers for \(h=2\) and empty for h>=4. A coordinate three-cycle fixes only points whose three permuted coordinates are simultaneously zero or one, leaving two lower-dimensional cubical two-skeleta. Actual packaged verifier checked all free pairs through \(n=5\) and 492 affine symmetry cases and independent three-cycle fixed-subcomplex homology through dimension five; finite checks corroborate but do not replace this parameter-uniform geometric proof.

value.rationale: The symmetric closed-neighborhood nerve is natural and its known wedge homotopy type does not reveal how the full affine group acts on points. The equivariant parity-lift cubical model captures every subgroup fixed-point homotopy type and provides an explicit uniform 2-dimensional geometric complex, with a nontrivial exact fixed-space classification for all coordinate three-cycles, including two disjoint sphere components at dimension five. The translation fixed-space count is corroborative, not a separate novelty assertion. This is substantive structural topology beyond covered rational characters, not a numerical increment or an arbitrary finite slice.
